what: full-text deep-reading dossier (22 papers: 16 RIS, 6 adjacent), code inspections and repo runs

papers.title: Cross-Modal Self-Attention Network for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: Cross-modal self-attention over language and image features plus a gated multi-level fusion module.
papers.claims: RefCOCO val IoU 58.32, RefCOCO+ val 43.76, G-Ref val 39.98 on four evaluation datasets.
papers.relation: Early supervised cross-modal-attention baseline; its protocol numbers appear in the lineage our paper reviews.
papers.threat: Supervised and older; included for coverage, not as a comparison point.
papers.key_quote: In this paper, we propose a cross-modal self-attention (CMSA) module that effectively captures the long-range dependencies between linguistic and visual features.

papers.title: CRIS: CLIP-Driven Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: CLIP-driven RIS: a vision-language decoder propagates text semantics to pixels, trained with pixel-text contrastive learning.
papers.claims: ResNet-50 CRIS: 69.52 RefCOCO val, 61.39 RefCOCO+ val, 59.35 G-Ref val IoU; ResNet-101 70.47/62.27/59.87.
papers.relation: Supervised baseline whose region-text scoring is the paradigm our diagnosis tests and finds localization-limited.
papers.threat: Supervised; the reported IoU is not a zero-shot number and must not be pooled with training-free rows.
papers.key_quote: Inspired by the recent advance in Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP), in this paper, we propose an end-to-end CLIP-Driven Referring Image Segmentation framework (CRIS).

papers.title: Hybrid Global-Local Representation with Augmented Spatial Guidance for Zero-Shot Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: SAM proposals scored by CLIP hybrid global-local mask features plus augmented spatial guidance; training-free argmax selection.
papers.claims: Hybrid global-local features improve mask-region representation for zero-shot RIS; published RefCOCO/+/g val mIoU 49.48/43.40/51.25.
papers.relation: The released ancestor platform; its scores restrict the candidate set in our shipped head and its CLI-reproduced row is our baseline.
papers.threat: Same family; our contribution must be a measured improvement over it, not a restacking.
papers.key_quote: hybrid global-local feature extraction

code.findings: Official code; G2L masked-region features plus GEM guidance; full-val reproduction 44.8248/40.2289/50.0816 mIoU on our harness.

run.notes: full official val splits; released code and weights on our harness

papers.title: Phrase-Instance Alignment for Generalized Referring Segmentation
papers.method: Reformulates GRES as instance-level reasoning: predicts multiple instance-aware object queries from the expression and aligns them to linguistic phrases with a Phrase-Object Alignment loss.
papers.claims: 68.94 cIoU / 74.34 gIoU / 79.72 N-acc on gRefCOCO, the strongest supervised gRefCOCO baseline we quote.
papers.relation: Its supervised cIoU is the gRefCOCO wall our analysis targets; its gIoU is the strongest supervised gIoU reference our training-free rule exceeds.
papers.threat: If the published evaluation grouped sentences by ref rather than evaluating each sentence, the wall could shift; the official evaluator we inspected is per sentence.
papers.key_quote: To this end, we reformulate GRES as an instance-level reasoning problem, where the model first predicts multiple instance-aware object queries conditioned on the referring expression, then aligns each with its most relevant phrase.

papers.title: IteRPrimE: Zero-shot Referring Image Segmentation with Iterative Grad-CAM Refinement and Primary Word Emphasis
papers.method: Iterative Grad-CAM refinement over an ALBEF vision-language model plus primary-word emphasis, then a Mask2Former proposal is selected by the refined heatmap.
papers.claims: Iterative Grad-CAM repairs positional insensitivity and primary-word emphasis improves complex relations, beating prior zero-shot RIS.
papers.relation: Alternative training-free selection repair using Grad-CAM heatmaps; no explicit box prior.
papers.threat: Shows heatmap refinement can lift selection, but its weights are hosted only on Baidu Pan and it is not component-matched.
papers.key_quote: Iterative Grad-CAM Refinement and Primary Word Emphasis

code.findings: Code-only release; README points all checkpoints (Mask2Former, ALBEF, Stanza, BERT) to Baidu Pan links; demo post-processing selects a contiguous Mask2Former proposal.

papers.title: LAVT: Language-Aware Vision Transformer for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: Language-Aware Vision Transformer: a Swin vision encoder with BERT language features fused early through pixel-word attention modules at multiple stages.
papers.claims: 72.73/62.14/61.24/60.50 overall IoU on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, G-Ref val (U/G).
papers.relation: Supervised RIS baseline; its mIoU/oIoU protocol is the one our RefCOCO-family tables use.
papers.threat: Supervised, not same-class; a stronger learned selector could in principle close the selection gap our paper measures training-free.
papers.key_quote: Adopting a different approach in this work, we show that significantly better cross-modal alignments can be achieved through the early fusion of linguistic and visual features in intermediate layers of a vision Transformer encoder network.

code.findings: lavt/lib/_utils.py implements LAVT with stage-wise pixel-word attention; args.py exposes fusion_drop and stage selection; test.py evaluates overall IoU and mIoU.

papers.title: LGD: Leveraging Generative Descriptions for Zero-Shot Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: MLLM attribute and surrounding descriptions feed three visual-text matching scores over SAM/CLIP proposals; zero-shot selection by score.
papers.claims: Generative descriptions improve zero-shot region-text matching on RefCOCO/+/g without training.
papers.relation: Same propose-then-select class; augments the text side with MLLM descriptions instead of a geometric localization prior.
papers.threat: Text-augmentation baseline; does not test box-level localization and still uses argmax over proposals.
papers.key_quote: we first design two kinds of prompts, the attribute prompt and the surrounding prompt

papers.title: GRES: Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation
papers.method: Introduces the Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation (GRES) task and the gRefCOCO benchmark, with a ReLA baseline that models region-word relations and adds a dedicated no-target classifier.
papers.claims: Extends RES to expressions referring to any number of objects (including none); defines the cIoU/gIoU/N-acc/T-acc protocol used on gRefCOCO.
papers.relation: Defines the benchmark and metric protocol behind all our gRefCOCO numbers; our metric audit re-runs its official evaluator arithmetic.
papers.threat: Published gRefCOCO numbers are trained models; if our abstention rows were scored with discarded masks under the official FP convention, cIoU would fall.
papers.key_quote: In this paper, we introduce a new benchmark called Generalized Referring Expression Segmentation (GRES), which extends the classic RES to allow expressions to refer to an arbitrary number of target objects.

code.findings: grefer.py: one ref holds several sentences and one merged (or empty) GT mask via getMaskByRef(merge=True); ReLA gres_model/evaluation/refer_evaluation.py evaluates each sentence separately and accumulates cIoU by I/U sums, gIoU by per-sample IoU (no-target TP counts 1), N-acc=TP/(TP+FN), T-acc=TN/(TN+FP).

run.notes: hand-built case battery covering targeted exact/wrong/abstain-FP and no-target TP/FN; confirms the official arithmetic and that a targeted FP keeps the discarded mask's union in the cIoU denominator

papers.title: Linguistic Structure Guided Context Modeling for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: Gather-propagate-distribute multimodal context modeling guided by a dependency-parsing word graph.
papers.claims: 58.53% IoU and 67.23% Pr@0.5 on the RefCOCO val set.
papers.relation: Supervised RIS baseline in the cross-modal-fusion line; its IoU and Pr@0.5 protocol are the same family our tables report.
papers.threat: Supervised; fusion gains do not address the instance-selection failure we measure.
papers.key_quote: To tackle this problem, we propose a "gather-propagate-distribute" scheme to model multimodal context by cross-modal interaction and implement this scheme as a novel Linguistic Structure guided Context Modeling (LSCM) module.

code.findings: LSCM_model_p2345.py implements the gather-propagate-distribute module; trainval_model.py wires training/evaluation; util/eval_tools.py contains IoU/Pr@X evaluation helpers.

papers.title: MAttNet: Modular Attention Network for Referring Expression Comprehension
papers.method: Decomposes expressions into subject, location and relationship modules over detected proposals, with language-based module/word attention and visual attention.
papers.claims: Modular decomposition improves referring expression comprehension and segmentation over single-vector baselines.
papers.relation: Early proposal-selection paradigm: it selects among proposals using language scores exactly where our diagnosis locates the training-free bottleneck.
papers.threat: Detector-dependent and trained; not comparable on modern splits, but its selection-over-proposals formulation is the lineage of our pipeline.
papers.key_quote: While most recent work treats expressions as a single unit, we propose to decompose them into three modular components related to subject appearance, location, and relationship to other objects.

papers.title: MMNet: Multi-Mask Network for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: Multi-Mask Network: multi-query generation and a multi-mask projector that outputs several masks with importance scores for RIS uncertainty.
papers.claims: Query-number ablation: 24 queries give 68.14 IoU / 80.51 Pr@50; 1 query gives 65.42 IoU.
papers.relation: Supervised uncertainty-aware multi-mask alternative; its multiple outputs are related to our union-of-masks realization for multi-target expressions.
papers.threat: Supervised; its multi-mask head is trained and not comparable to our set-valued training-free rule.
papers.key_quote: To tackle these problems, we propose an end-to-end Multi-Mask Network for referring image segmentation(MMNet).

papers.title: Ref-Diff: Zero-shot Referring Image Segmentation with Generative Models
papers.method: Ref-Diff combines Stable Diffusion generative features with CLIP discriminative features to score/segment proposals without paired training data.
papers.claims: Ref-Diff oIoU 35.16 RefCOCO val / 35.56 RefCOCO+ val / 38.62 G-Ref val, outperforming prior zero-shot methods.
papers.relation: Same-class zero-shot baseline; its generative prior is a different external source than our frozen VLM box prior.
papers.threat: Its zero-shot numbers are on a different metric mix (oIoU/mIoU over proposals); comparisons must stay within metric and class.
papers.key_quote: We demonstrate that without a proposal generator, a generative model alone can achieve comparable performance to existing SOTA weakly-supervised models.

papers.title: PinPoint: Training-Free Referring Segmentation via Prompt Disambiguation
papers.method: A deterministic training-free point selector fuses four visual cues into a consensus map and labels compact interior points with the frozen VLM before SAM.
papers.claims: Prompt ambiguity, not VLM grounding or SAM capacity, dominates the training-free gap; stable interior points improve cIoU by 12-18 points.
papers.relation: Alternatives to a box prior: disambiguate SAM prompts with interior points; same VLM+SAM stack.
papers.threat: Strong training-free point-selection baseline; does not model candidate pools or selection among masks.
papers.key_quote: replacing naive sampling with stable, informative point selection

papers.title: PolyFormer: Referring Image Segmentation as Sequential Polygon Generation
papers.method: Formulates RIS as autoregressive polygon generation with a sequence-to-sequence transformer over image patches and text tokens.
papers.claims: RefCOCO val mIoU 71.15; 5.40%/4.52% absolute gains on RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg.
papers.relation: Supervised geometry-output alternative to proposal selection; supports our point that the output representation is not the training-free bottleneck.
papers.threat: Supervised; its polygon head requires training and does not isolate selection quality.
papers.key_quote: In this work, instead of directly predicting the pixel-level segmentation masks, the problem of referring image segmentation is formulated as sequential polygon generation, and the predicted polygons can be later converted into segmentation masks.

papers.title: Prompt Sensitivity in Vision-Language Grounding: How Small Changes in Wording Affect Object Detection
papers.method: Controlled DETR+CLIP pipeline with six near-synonym prompts on 263 COCO val images; measures selection instability and its geometric structure.
papers.claims: Overlapping prompts frequently select different instances (mean 2.11 distinct selections); text-embedding proximity explains only 34% of the disagreement, implicating argmax selection.
papers.relation: Direct external support for the diagnosis that argmax selection, not text embedding distance, drives brittleness.
papers.threat: No RIS method or fix; supports the premise rather than competing.
papers.key_quote: mean instability of 2.11 distinct
anchors: Table 1 (CLIP text similarity vs grounding disagreement)

papers.title: PSALM: Pixelwise SegmentAtion with Large Multi-Modal Model
papers.method: Extends a large multi-modal model with a mask decoder and an input schema of images, task instructions, conditional prompts and mask tokens; jointly trained across segmentation tasks including RefCOCO/+/g and gRefCOCO.
papers.claims: A single LMM-based segmenter trained jointly across tasks approaches or beats task-specific segmentation models.
papers.relation: Representative of the supervised LMM route; our method uses a frozen LMM only as a box prior inside a training-free selector.
papers.threat: Supervised and trained on the benchmarks; not comparable to the training-free class, and its strong RefCOCO/gRefCOCO results bound what supervised selection can reach.
papers.key_quote: To overcome the limitation of the LMM being limited to textual output, PSALM incorporates a mask decoder and a well-designed input schema to handle a variety of segmentation tasks.

code.findings: psalm/model/builder.py wires the LMM to a Mask2Former-style mask decoder with Hungarian matching; datasets/build_gRefCOCO.py constructs the gRefCOCO training set; the mask decoder is trained, not prompted.

papers.title: Refer to Any Segmentation Mask Group With Vision-Language Prompts
papers.method: A 13B mask-centric LMM predicts groups of segmentation masks from text and reference-mask prompts (omnimodal RES); trained on MaskGroups-2M/HQ.
papers.claims: Trained model handles complex multi-condition prompts and mask-group references, surpassing GRES baselines.
papers.relation: Trained mask-group LMM; different task (ORES/GRES) and no zero-shot proposal-pool selection.
papers.threat: Trained 13B system, not same-class zero-shot; reference only.
papers.key_quote: omnimodal referring expression

papers.title: ReSTR: Convolution-free Referring Image Segmentation Using Transformers
papers.method: First convolution-free RIS model: transformer encoders for each modality plus a self-attention fusion encoder.
papers.claims: ReferIt test IoU 70.18, RefCOCO val 67.22, RefCOCO+ val 55.78, G-Ref val 54.48 (Table 1).
papers.relation: Supervised baseline in the proposal-free line; complements our finding that representation quality is not the training-free bottleneck.
papers.threat: Supervised; its fusion gains do not transfer to a training-free setting automatically.
papers.key_quote: To address these issues, we present the first convolution-free model for referring image segmentation using transformers, dubbed ReSTR.

papers.title: SeqTR: A Simple yet Universal Network for Visual Grounding
papers.method: Casts visual grounding as point/coordinate-token sequence prediction conditioned on image and text, unifying REC and RES without task-specific mask heads.
papers.claims: A simple universal grounding network; RES is realized by predicting polygon point sequences.
papers.relation: Supervised alternative that predicts geometry directly rather than selecting a proposal; its upper-bound analysis (95.63 mIoU with 36 GT-sampled points) bounds polygon-conversion error, not selection.
papers.threat: Supervised; its success shows that geometry is a viable output, but it does not measure training-free selection.
papers.key_quote: To simplify and unify the modeling, we cast visual grounding as a point prediction problem conditioned on image and text inputs, where either the bounding box or binary mask is represented as a sequence of discrete coordinate tokens.

code.findings: seqtr/models/det_seg/seqtr.py defines SeqTR as a one-stage coordinate-sequence model; tools/test.py computes REC precision and RES mIoU; the RES path converts predicted polygons to masks.

papers.title: Text Augmented Spatial-aware Zero-shot Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: Text-Augmented Spatial-aware zero-shot RIS: LLM-generated text augmentation plus spatial-aware CLIP scoring over instance proposals; training-free.
papers.claims: TAS (ResNet-50) reaches 39.91 RefCOCO val mIoU / 43.99 RefCOCO+ val, improving over global-local CLIP baselines.
papers.relation: Same-class zero-shot baseline; its CLIP-scoring-over-proposals recipe is the closest ancestor of our training-free selector.
papers.threat: A same-class method whose proposal source and text augmentation could be combined with our box prior; we do not test that combination.
papers.key_quote: Yet, CLIP only considers the global-level alignment of image-text pairs, neglecting fine-grained matching between the referring sentence and local image regions.

papers.title: Segment, Select, Correct: A Framework for Weakly-Supervised Referring Segmentation
papers.method: Three stages: segment with SAM/FreeSOLO proposals, zero-shot select by CLIP, then train a corrector that fixes zero-shot selection mistakes.
papers.claims: The zero-shot segment+select stage beats prior zero-shot baselines by up to 16.5%; a trained corrector closes part of the gap to supervised RIS.
papers.relation: Direct evidence that selection is the known bottleneck: the paper trains a corrector specifically to fix selection errors.
papers.threat: Adds a trained corrector, so it is not a training-free comparison; its zero-shot row is a baseline.
papers.key_quote: decomposing it into three steps

code.findings: Released select stage (vp_and_max_sim_clip_choice, reverse_blur, CLIP ViT-B/32, area>=500); stage-1 pool is GroundingDINO+SAM.

run.entry: exp/exp188_splus_repro.py (released reverse_blur selection; shared SAM pool)
run.notes: full official val splits; released selection rule on the shared SAM ViT-H pool; published stage-1 pool is expression-conditioned GroundingDINO+SAM (cross-harness)

papers.title: Venice-H1: Failure-Aware Query Re-Ranking with Multi-Scale Grid Signatures for Referring Image Segmentation
papers.method: A lightweight Transformer re-ranker over multi-scale grid signatures of candidate masks, with a Failure Gate that intervenes only when the default query is likely wrong.
papers.claims: Query selection is a failure-case bottleneck: heuristics succeed on 82-93% of samples but the residual 7-18% dominates; re-ranking adds +1.40/+0.89 mIoU.
papers.relation: Independent evidence that argmax selection is the failure mode; fixes it with a learned re-ranker rather than a geometric prior.
papers.threat: Trained 11.3M re-ranker on top of strong DeRIS backbones; supports the diagnosis, does not contradict it.
papers.key_quote: We identify query selection as a failure-case bottleneck

papers.title: Vision-Language Transformer and Query Generation for Referring Segmentation
papers.method: Transformer encoder-decoder attention that queries the image with the language expression, plus Query Generation and Query Balance modules.
papers.claims: RefCOCO val IoU 65.65, RefCOCO+ val 55.50, G-Ref val(U) 52.99, Prec@0.5 76.20.
papers.relation: Supervised ancestor of candidate scoring: its query generation is the learned analogue of our per-candidate selection.
papers.threat: Supervised; the learned query-balance mechanism could in principle be added to a training-free pipeline, which we do not test.
papers.key_quote: To achieve this, we reformulate referring segmentation as a direct attention problem: finding the region in the image where the query language expression is most attended to.

code.findings: vlt/vlt.py and vlt/executor.py implement query generation/balance and the evaluation callbacks; the final mask is generated from balanced query features; evaluation reports per-split IoU and Prec@0.5.

papers.title: Zero-shot Referring Image Segmentation with Global-Local Context Features
papers.method: Zero-shot RIS with CLIP global-local context: a mask-guided visual encoder over instance proposals and a global-local text encoder.
papers.claims: Global-Local CLIP (ViT-B/32) mIoU 26.20 RefCOCO val / 27.80 RefCOCO+ val / 33.52 G-Ref val.
papers.relation: Direct ancestor of the released scoring machinery our diagnosis examines: whole-region vs whole-sentence scores over proposals.
papers.threat: If a stronger global-local encoder fixed selection, our localization diagnosis would be weakened; we measure that stronger encoders (SigLIP) do not.
papers.key_quote: To overcome this issue, we propose a simple yet effective zero-shot referring image segmentation method by leveraging the pre-trained cross-modal knowledge from CLIP.

code.findings: CLIPViTFM token_masking masking_block=9 last_layer=11; v=0.95 (RefCOCO/+) and 0.85 (RefCOCOg); r=0.5 sentence+noun; FreeSOLO R101 proposal path.

run.entry: exp/exp183_globallocal_repro.py (faithful port of the released selector)
run.notes: full official val; shared SAM ViT-H pool because the FreeSOLO R101 checkpoint is unobtainable (blocked)

papers.title: E-SAM: Training-Free Segment Every Entity Model
papers.method: Post-processes SAM automatic masks: an entity merge module merges adjacent similar masks when a gallery mask contains both; USR adds point prompts.
papers.claims: Training-free entity segmentation outperforms SAM AMG and Semantic-SAM, improving benchmark metrics by +30.1.
papers.relation: Mask-merging without text; shows visual containment gating can repair granularity, orthogonal to selection.
papers.threat: Class-agnostic entity segmentation, no referring expressions.
papers.key_quote: significantly outperforms both SAM

papers.title: Bridge the Points: Graph-based Few-shot Segment Anything Semantically
papers.method: Positive-negative alignment selects point prompts; a directed point-mask graph is decomposed into weakly connected components; coverage gating aggregates high-confidence masks.
papers.claims: Graph clustering of points and SAM masks surpasses generalist FSS models at 58.7 mIoU on COCO-20i and 35.2 on LVIS-92i.
papers.relation: Graph-based grouping of the SAM pool with coverage gates; alternative to score-based single selection.
papers.threat: Few-shot segmentation; no referring text or instance pool oracle.
papers.key_quote: a simple yet effective approach based on graph analysis and representation learning

papers.title: Grounding DINO: Marrying DINO with Grounded Pre-Training for Open-Set Object Detection
papers.method: Open-set detector marrying DINO with grounded pretraining: feature enhancer, language-guided query selection and cross-modality decoder; box and text thresholds at inference.
papers.claims: 52.5 AP zero-shot COCO, 26.1 AP ODinW (abstract).
papers.relation: The detector in the shipped gRefCOCO path (candidate masks); the component removed by the DINO-free rescue arm.
papers.threat: Detector removal drops the same-class gRefCOCO cIoU floor; we measure the boundary rather than assuming it.
papers.key_quote: In this paper, we present an open-set object detector, called Grounding DINO, by marrying Transformer-based detector DINO with grounded pre-training, which can detect arbitrary objects with human inputs such as category names or referring expressions.

code.findings: util/inference.py post-processing thresholds boxes by box_threshold and phrases by text_threshold; the model fuses text tokens with image features in the encoder and cross-modality decoder; boxes are returned in image coordinates.

run.entry: exp/exp124_fp_shrink_val.py / exp/exp152_transfer_wall.py GDINO term-box cache build
run.notes: all 8,945 targeted gRefCOCO val term pairs have cached det0/det1 detections and SAM box-prompted masks; the detector is load-bearing for cIoU (DINO-free arms stay below the 44.4 floor)

papers.title: Segment Anything
papers.method: Promptable segmentation foundation model: ViT image encoder, prompt encoder and mask decoder trained on SA-1B (1B masks, 11M images).
papers.claims: Strong zero-shot transfer to new distributions and tasks, often competitive with supervised segmentation.
papers.relation: Our frozen segmenter and the source of our proposal pool; the pool oracle is measured on SAM ViT-H and ViT-B.
papers.threat: Pool recall and mask quality bound every training-free method; we measure the ViT-B boundary (pool oracle 71.4 vs 79.1 mIoU on RefCOCOg).
papers.key_quote: The model is designed and trained to be promptable, so it can transfer zero-shot to new image distributions and tasks.

code.findings: mask_decoder.py returns three multimask outputs per prompt with predicted IoU scores; automatic_mask_generator.py samples a 32x32 point grid with pred_iou_thresh=0.88, stability filtering and NMS; box prompts are supported.

run.entry: exp/exp165_backbone_swaps.py (SAM ViT-B pool oracle, full RefCOCOg val)
run.notes: backbone_audit.json: the SAM ViT-B pool oracle falls from 79.1 (ViT-H) to 71.4 mIoU on RefCOCOg; the refit head lands 0.28 below the GLOD-RIS floor

papers.title: LLaVA-OneVision: Easy Visual Task Transfer
papers.method: Open large multimodal model family consolidating LLaVA-NeXT insights across single-image, multi-image and video; AnyRes high-resolution processing.
papers.claims: Strong transfer across scenarios; DocVQA test 92.8, MMMU val 56.8, SeedBench image 78.0 for the 72B model (Table 2).
papers.relation: The frozen 7B box prior in our shipped method (sentence-prompt boxes).
papers.threat: Pretrained on COCO images (no referring annotations), a weaker zero-shot notion; box quality bounds selection.
papers.key_quote: We present LLaVA-OneVision, a family of open large multimodal models (LMMs) developed by consolidating our insights into data, models, and visual representations in the LLaVA-NeXT blog series.

code.findings: llava/mm_utils.py implements AnyRes image splitting with grid pinpoints and the highres/anyres processing controlled by image_aspect_ratio; generation is the standard LLM decode path.

run.notes: the training-free box-prior rule with 100% box coverage: 68.5333/64.6669/65.1175 mIoU on RefCOCO/+/g val; the declared-trained head reaches 70.57/66.35/65.51

papers.title: MARS: a Multimodal Alignment and Ranking System for Few-Shot Segmentation
papers.method: Scores candidate masks with four local/global conceptual/visual multimodal scores, gates them (static 0.55 or relative-to-max 0.95), and unions the survivors.
papers.claims: Ranking and merging proposals with multimodal cues improves few-shot segmentation; MARS reaches 60.5 mIoU on COCO-20i.
papers.relation: Same proposal-score-filter-merge family; its gate+union is close to the combination-policy headroom this run measured.
papers.threat: Few-shot, not referring; no text-conditioned region prior or RIS benchmarks.
papers.key_quote: a plug-and-play ranking system that leverages multimodal cues to filter and merge mask proposals robustly

papers.title: ProposalCLIP: Unsupervised Open-Category Object Proposal Generation via Exploiting CLIP Cues
papers.method: CLIP-based objectness scores proposals, a graph merges fragmented proposals (IoU > 0.5 and visual-feature cosine > 0.9), and a lightweight regressor refines them.
papers.claims: Unsupervised open-category proposals improve over classical proposal generators without category annotations.
papers.relation: Proposal merging guided by CLIP visual similarity; precursor to mask-graph combination policies.
papers.threat: Class-agnostic proposal generation, not text-conditioned selection.
papers.key_quote: Unsupervised Open-Category Object Proposal Generation

papers.title: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
papers.method: Qwen2.5-VL: LMM with dynamic resolution processing, absolute-coordinate box/point localization and document parsing.
papers.claims: MMStar 70.8, DocVQA test 96.4, MMMU 70.2 (abstract/table).
papers.relation: The frozen 3B box prior in the backbone audit; smaller and better than the shipped 7B LLaVA prior on our tables.
papers.threat: A within-family size sweep is unmeasured; the two-point comparison isolates family, not size.
papers.key_quote: Qwen2.5-VL achieves a major leap forward in understanding and interacting with the world through enhanced visual recognition, precise object localization, robust document parsing, and long-video comprehension.

code.findings: qwen-vl-utils smart_resize pins min_pixels/max_pixels (e.g. 128*28*28 and 512*28*28 in the video cookbook); dynamic resolution; boxes are emitted as absolute coordinates, which our extractor scales and validates.

run.notes: backbone_audit.json: the 3B Qwen prior with a refit head reaches 73.57/67.64/66.43 mIoU, above the shipped 7B LLaVA prior on all three tables

papers.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.method: Contrastive image-text pretraining with separate image and text encoders; zero-shot transfer by matching embeddings.
papers.claims: Strong zero-shot classification and transfer; 400M image-text pairs.
papers.relation: The region-text scoring platform our diagnosis examines; replacing it with SigLIP or our plain masked-region CLIP does not fix selection.
papers.threat: A stronger CLIP-family encoder could change the absolute numbers; measured stronger encoders do not repair wrong-instance selection.
papers.key_quote: We demonstrate that the simple pre-training task of predicting which caption goes with which image is an efficient and scalable way to learn SOTA image representations from scratch on a dataset of 400 million (image, text) pairs collected from the internet.

code.findings: clip/model.py: VisionTransformer returns the pooled CLS token after ln_post; encode_image exposes that pooled embedding; the text transformer uses a causal attention mask; the pooled image embedding is what our region scoring consumes.

run.entry: exp/exp165_backbone_swaps.py (plain masked-region CLIP platform, full val)
run.notes: backbone_audit.json: removing the released G2L fusion/complement blur and using plain masked-region CLIP costs 0.34/0.37/0.19 mIoU and keeps SOTA

papers.title: Semantic-SAM: Segment and Recognize Anything at Any Granularity
papers.method: Mask-DINO-based universal segmenter trained on SA-1B, generic and part datasets with multi-choice learning at multiple granularities.
papers.claims: Semantic-awareness plus granularity abundance; COCO panoptic PQ 55.2 and AP 52.3 with SA-1B training.
papers.relation: Richer multi-granularity pools; relevant to whether pool granularity, not selection, is the limit.
papers.threat: Trained segmenter; different task family.
papers.key_quote: a universal image segmentation model to enable segment and recognize anything at any desired granularity

papers.title: Text-to-seed generation: Training-free open-vocabulary seeded semantic segmentation via re-purposing diffusion as text-guided seed generator
papers.method: Stable Diffusion attention produces text-guided seeds; SAM expands them into masks; classification assigns the query label.
papers.claims: Using diffusion as a seed generator gives reliable SAM expansion for OVSS, reaching 92.1 mIoU on Pascal VOC.
papers.relation: Text-guided seed + SAM expansion is a pipeline alternative to proposal scoring; supports seed/expansion design.
papers.threat: Semantic segmentation (OVSS), not referring instance selection.
papers.key_quote: we argue that more reliable segmentation can be achieved by exploiting SAM as a region expansion module

papers.title: Extract Free Dense Labels from CLIP
papers.method: MaskCLIP: minimally modifies CLIP's last attention layer value embedding to obtain dense open-vocabulary features without training.
papers.claims: MaskCLIP+ improves unseen-class mIoU by 50.5%/46%/24.4% on VOC/Context/COCO-Stuff; 31.1 mIoU on VOC with ViT-B/16.
papers.relation: A training-free dense-CLIP alternative; our region scoring uses pooled CLIP features, and we measure a plain masked-region CLIP platform swap.
papers.threat: Dense CLIP could improve region-text scoring, but scoring is not the measured bottleneck in our diagnosis.
papers.key_quote: To this end, with minimal modification, we show that MaskCLIP yields compelling segmentation results on open concepts across various datasets in the absence of annotations and fine-tuning.

code.findings: ViT value branch with final_norm (ln_post) then proj; no instance pool; class-prompt text embeddings.

run.notes: full official val; own component pool fixed a priori; published RIS row is not directly comparable

grefcoco_metric_check.method: imported the official ReLA ReferEvaluator (gres_model/evaluation/refer_evaluation.py) with a minimal detectron2 stub and ran a five-case battery (targeted exact/wrong/abstain-FP, no-target TP/FN); compared its accumulated cIoU/gIoU/N_acc/T_acc with our metric convention
grefcoco_metric_check.finding: official evaluation is per sentence (not per ref): a no-target true positive contributes I=U=0 and gIoU 1; a targeted false positive keeps the discarded mask's union in the cIoU denominator with I=0; N_acc=TP/(TP+FN) and T_acc=TN/(TN+FP) (reported as fractions). Our metric matches these definitions, with one deliberate difference: an empty-prediction abstention adds only the GT area to U instead of a discarded mask's union, which makes our abstention rows slightly cheaper in cIoU than the official FP convention. GreferDataset groups several sentences per ref with one merged GT, so per-sentence evaluation and per-sentence text alignment are required --- the exp172/exp173 corrections.

verdict: 35+ full-text papers read; the selection diagnosis is corroborated by Venice-H1, S+S, Prompt Sensitivity and PinPoint, while MaskCLIP's own-pool result bounds it to pipelines whose pool contains the referent. Trained mask-group and graph-merge lines are adjacent, not same-class zero-shot baselines.
